notes: Account summary: mid-stage procurement for Dedicated + Private control plane. Heavy compliance needs, finance team focused on predictable unit economics.
Primary use-case: low-latency chat assistant for customer support + nightly reranking jobs for personalization. Embeddings used for similarity and fraud detection.
Performance targets: p95 latency <= 120ms for 1-2k concurrent chat streams (avg message length ~40 tokens). Bulk reranking throughput target: 10k qps (batched).
Reserved GPU planning: asking for an initial commit equivalent to 8x A100-class GPUs (model: LlamaX-13B quantized) with headroom for burst to 12 GPUs during promotions.
Routing/fallback: primary route to Dedicated pool; fallback to hosted-compatible quantized variants in another region for degraded capacity. Must preserve privacy controls when falling back.
SLA asks (customer): 99.99% uptime, proactive maintenance notices 30d, credits for partial outages, 1hr severity 1 response (phone), 24/7 escalation path.

Redwood proposed SLA: 99.95% uptime for Dedicated baseline; credit schedule tiered (see below); maintenance windows limited to 4h monthly with 21d calendar notice; 2hr S1 response and 24/7 on-call escalation.

Proposed credit schedule (negotiation starting point): <99.95% -> 10% monthly credit; <99.9% -> 25% monthly credit; <99.5% -> 50% + dedicated remediation runbook & waiver. Customer pushing for steeper credits; legal prefers banded approach.
Maintenance window preference: customer prefers Sunday 02:00-05:00 UTC (low traffic) and requires ability to opt-out for major product launches (blackout dates).
Support and runbook: customer requires runbook access, weekly incident drills during pilot, and a dedicated SE for first 90 days. SE (Anika) committed to on-site kickoff.
Data residency: core inference logs must remain within us-east-1. Audit logs retained for 7 years per compliance team request — Redwood retention add-on needed.

POC plan: 4-week pilot, week1 capacity baseline + perf tuning; week2 load test (2k concurrent chats p95 target), week3 fault-injection and failover; week4 runbook handover + cost optimization recommendations.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-20): "We need guarantees; if you can show consistent 99.95% and demonstrable token-cost reductions, we can expand to 24/7 support use cases."
Finance: prefers monthly billing but open to 12-month reserved commitment if credits/penalties favorable. Wants clarity on partial-credit proration per outage window.
Legal notes: pushing back on 'reasonable efforts' language for backup and failover; requests explicit measurable SLOs and defined change-control for maintenance.
Technical risks: on-prem certification for air-gapped environment will add 6-10 weeks; encryption key custody (HSM) integration scheduled but needs KMS proof-of-concept.
Decision criteria: uptime SLO acceptance, credit schedule alignment, clear operational playbook (runbooks + on-call), confirmed cost per 1M tokens under reserved plan.
Next ask: Redwood to produce redlined SLA + example credit calculation spreadsheet by 2026-03-15. Legal call scheduled 2026-03-12.
Internal AE notes: prioritize showing 3rd-party perf benchmarks for similarly sized deployments; emphasize Optimize recommendations to control unit economics.
